selection_reasoning: These 4 tasks form a coherent multi-hop dependency chain. The player must first 'find wheat' to locate wheat in the environment, which can be used to lure/breed rabbits or as a trading resource. 'Hunt a rabbit' requires knowing the area (finding wheat fields often means open areas where rabbits spawn). 'Craft to iron_bars' requires iron ingots which the player needs to locate/mine, and this crafting demonstrates resource processing. Finally, 'trade for iron chestplate' requires finding a villager (armorer) and having emeralds - the iron bars can be traded to a villager for emeralds, and wheat can also be sold to farmer villagers for emeralds, which are then used to purchase the iron chestplate. This creates a meaningful dependency structure where resource gathering feeds into trading.

Rabbit hide (4) can be traded to leatherworker villagers for emeralds toward chestplate purchase

milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because 'find wheat' is an observation/locate task. The player must navigate near the wheat field (centered at spawn-relative [-3, 1, -3]) and face toward it, modeling 'player can see the wheat.' Max distance 16 blocks with 60° facing tolerance ensures the player has actually located and observed the wheat.

Uses count_in_box_at_most with kind='mob' and max_count=2 because hunting a rabbit means killing at least one of the 3 rabbits in the pen. The generous box (±15 around the rabbit pen center at [5,1,3]) ensures all rabbits remain inside the detection area until actually killed. If count drops from 3 to at most 2, at least one rabbit has been killed.

Uses inventory_has because crafting iron bars results in the item appearing in the player's inventory. The recipe yields 16 iron bars from 6 iron ingots, and the player starts with no iron bars, so having at least 1 iron_bars confirms successful crafting. Using min_count=1 to be lenient (player may place some).

Uses inventory_has because trading for an iron chestplate results in the item appearing in the player's inventory. The player starts with no iron chestplate, so having at least 1 confirms a successful trade with the armorer villager.
